title: Choose the new look for BizEazy Hub
question: The roll assigned the expressway-signage world. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Expressway Signage
options.lineage: Malaysian JKR and expressway direction signs
options.thesis: Read your business like the highway: what's ahead, how far away, and the next exit.
materials: retroreflective sign panels with an inset white border
options.viewport: A green direction panel opens the Hub: RM owed and RM collected this month in heavy white figures; below, a yellow 'needs you' strip ranked by days left (Salary · 2 days); quick actions as exit tabs: New invoice, New quote, Run payroll.
options.risk: Tips into theme-park kitsch if sign shapes become decoration, and its green must not read like the old pine.

raised.raise: Colour carries state, not borders: a green, yellow or red panel IS the status, so outlines and boxes go.
Every record leads with its reference number, set like an exit number.
Figure size follows importance on one fixed ramp: what you are owed is always the biggest number on screen.
Lifecycles read on one fixed strip: quote, invoice, part paid, paid, in the same positions everywhere.

options.label: Kitchen Ticket Rail
options.lineage: order tickets clipped at the pass, thermal receipts
options.thesis: Everything that needs you hangs on the rail like orders waiting at the pass.
options.viewport: Today's tickets clipped along a rail across the top (Salary due, Invoice overdue), with this month's money printed below like a receipt's total line.
options.risk: Receipt paper and monospace are a familiar retro-POS trope, and long lists can feel cramped.

options.label: Departures Board
options.lineage: airport and rail split-flap departure boards
options.thesis: Deadlines as departures: rows ranked by time, each one boarding, delayed or gone.
options.viewport: A board of rows (SALARY SEPT · DUE 7 OCT · BOARDING) ranked by time, with money in the header strip.
options.case: Fuses well on clarity, as deadlines map onto departures; loses on recognition and on reading money on a black board in daylight.
options.risk: A dark board is hard to read in a bright restaurant, and flap animation must never slow anything down.

options.label: Streaming Rows
options.thesis: Rows you swipe sideways: branches, customers and staff as tiles that grow when you land on them.
options.viewport: Horizontal rows (Owed to you, Due this week, Your branches) with the focused tile expanding to show its figures.
options.case: Everyone knows the gesture; but restaurant records have no artwork, so tiles go empty and lose on clarity.
options.risk: Sideways scrolling hides money and deadlines off screen.

options.label: Metro Tiles
options.thesis: Giant lowercase type and flat colour tiles, no chrome.
options.viewport: Tiles as doors to each module.
options.case: Cropped giant type fights legible money.
options.risk: Reads as a dated phone OS.
options.kept: Colour fields carry state; boxes and outlines go.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything numbered, meaning coded in colour strips.
options.viewport: A numbered index as the only map.
options.case: Coded meaning hides what an owner must read at a glance.
options.risk: Too cryptic for a busy owner.
options.kept: The reference number leads every record.

options.label: Star Atlas
options.thesis: Importance drawn as size on a fixed scale.
options.viewport: Customers plotted by what they owe.
options.case: Beautiful, but nobody runs a restaurant by star chart.
options.kept: Figure size follows importance on one fixed ramp.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: One subject followed through its stages at a fixed scale.
options.viewport: A quotation followed from draft to paid.
options.case: Cream and serif is the default look this round must avoid.
options.risk: Precious and slow for a working tool.
options.kept: Lifecycles on one fixed-position stage strip.

canonCard.label: Modern business-app standard
canonCard.thesis: What well-made business apps ship: clean, calm, familiar.
canonCard.viewport: Summary cards for owed and collected, a to-do list, and buttons for quick actions.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every other business app by design.
